correctness.rationale: With half graph edges a_i b_j iff i<=j, b1 and a_n are leaves. Under the zero-neighborhood sum>=2 rule, an unpressed leaf forces its unique neighbor label 2; its quasi-total positive-neighbor rule costs a further unit. The opposite leaf similarly imposes a >=4 budget for n>=3. Endpoint and nested-neighborhood deductions show weight-4 labelings for n>=4 cannot have either leaf positive (any alternative exhausts the remaining budget before internal zeros are defended); thus exactly a1=bn=2 occurs. The exceptional n=2 and n=3 exhaustive optimizer lists have respectively 2 and 4 members; minimum weights 3 and 4. Independently enumerated all ternary labelings for n=2..6; optimizer counts 2,4,1,1,1 and no lower weight. The published identity gamma_I*+partial_s*=|V| gives strong differential 1 (n=2) and 2n-4 for n>=3.
